account:
This morning I read my updated appointments: office at eight, mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea with my neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, and the innkeeper's great-hall meeting at eighteen. I am specifically asked not to arrive early, and the secretary says they will escort me at precisely eighteen hundred. That insistence is unusual, as is the amount of preparation for a meeting whose business has not been explained to me.

Builder reported twenty-four loaves delivered to the hall yesterday. Builder, freight, and innkeeper have coordinated supplies, with building materials exchanged for grain; my secretary saw materials handed over. I also saw a lantern installed in the hall yesterday. My neighbour has met the same people and offered to help with baking, though I do not know whether that offer led to anything. This morning the innkeeper explicitly said they requested the bread for committee hospitality and that it is reserved for tonight's meeting. That answers who requested it and its stated use, but not which committee is meeting or what it plans to discuss. I have just asked the secretary for the committee's identity and any agenda or letters.

My best guess is that people are jointly preparing a gathering with food, perhaps something more social than an ordinary business appointment. The unexplained purpose and request not to arrive early could mean they want the preparations kept from me, possibly for a surprise, but I have no confirmation. I have no evidence of wrongdoing or unauthorized treasury spending: yesterday the treasury contained 128 emeralds untouched, and the secretary authorized no bread order. I should distinguish their observed cooperation from my suspicions, keep today's appointments, and hear what the secretary can actually establish.
